title: Slow-Roasted Greek Lamb Shoulder with Garlic and Lemon
summary: Tender lamb shoulder roasted low and slow with garlic, lemon, oregano and rosemary for a classic Greek-style dinner. The meat turns deeply savoury and fragrant, with bright citrus cutting through the richness.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Pat the lamb shoulder dry and place it in a roasting tin or deep baking dish.
Make small slits all over the lamb with a sharp knife. Push the garlic into the slits, then rub the meat with olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, oregano, rosemary, salt and black pepper.
Scatter the sliced onion around the lamb and pour the water into the base of the tin. Cover tightly with foil or a lid.
Roast for 3 hours, basting once or twice with the juices, until the lamb is very tender and starting to pull apart.
Remove the foil, increase the oven to 220°C, and roast for 20 to 30 minutes more until the outside is browned and lightly crisp.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes before carving or shredding. Spoon the pan juices over the meat and serve hot with potatoes, rice or a Greek salad if you like.
